chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and ʿAli ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Sayqal, from his father, who said:
I, al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah, and a group of our companions were sitting, while Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام was listening to our conversation, so he said to us: “What matter are you engaged in?”

Far be it, far be it! No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass until you are sifted. No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass until you are thoroughly tested. No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass until you are distinguished from one another. No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass except after despair. No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass until the one who is to be wretched becomes wretched, and the one who is to be felicitous becomes felicitous.

key_terms.إِيَاسٍ: Despair; the awaited matter will only occur after people reach a state of hopelessness.
key_terms.تُغَرْبَلُوا: You are sifted; meaning the community will be screened and separated through trials.
key_terms.تُمَحَّصُوا: You are purified and tested intensely, so that sincerity is distinguished from insincerity.
key_terms.تُمَيَّزُوا: You are differentiated from one another; people become clearly distinct in their true states.
key_terms.هَيْهَاتَ: An expression of remoteness, indicating that the awaited matter is still far off.
key_terms.يَسْعَدَ: Becomes felicitous; the condition of those destined for happiness and success becomes manifest.
key_terms.يَشْقَى: Becomes wretched; the condition of those destined for misery becomes manifest.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about trials and purification before the awaited matter occurs?
ai.summary: This hadith describes Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام informing his companions that the matter they await will not occur until a period of severe trial, purification, and clear differentiation among people has taken place. It emphasizes sifting, testing, and despair before the final realization of the awaited matter, when the destined states of people become manifest.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Muhammad Bin Mansour Al Sayqal, from his father who said,
‘I and Haris Bin Al-Mugheira, and a group of our companions were seated, and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> heard our speech. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘In which thing (discussion) are you in?

Far be it! Far be it! No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! What you all are extending your eyes towards will not be happening until you are scrutinised! No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! What you are extending your eyes towards will not be happening until you are differentiated! No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! What you are extending your eyes towards will not be happening until after despair! No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! What you are extending your eyes towards will not be happening until the one who is a wretch becomes a wretch, and the one who is ‘يَسْعَدَ’ auspicious becomes auspicious’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan and Ali ibn Muhammad have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Sayqal from his father who has said the following.
“Once I, al-Harith ibn al-Mughira and a group of our people were in the presence of abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who could hear our conversations. He asked ask us, “What is the issue in your dialogue?

It will not happen and it will never happen. By Allah, what you are looking to will not take place before you are sifted, by Allah, what you are longing for will not happen until you are refined, by Allah, what you are looking will not happen before you are distinguished, by Allah, what you looking for will not take place before you despair, by Allah, what you are looking to will not take place before misfortune would strike those who become unfortunate and before the fortunate ones attain salvation.”
